faqs.q: How is weekly pay calculated from an annual salary?
faqs.a: Weekly pay is calculated by dividing the annual salary by 52. For a $90,000 salary, weekly gross pay is $1,730.77. After tax and Medicare, the weekly net is approximately $1,359. This assumes the full tax-free threshold and no other deductions.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For example, if your base rate is $45.55 per hour, casual loading brings it to $56.94 per hour. This is separate from super, which is paid on top of the loaded rate.

faqs.q: How much super is paid on top of my salary?
faqs.a: The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For a $90,000 annual salary, that's an extra $10,800 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not included in your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your 90k After Tax Australia Weekly Salary

If you're looking for your **90k after tax Australia weekly salary**, you've come to the right place. This guide breaks down how a $90,000 annual salary converts to hourly, weekly, and fortnightly pay, including tax, super, and casual loading. We use the standard 38-hour week and the latest 2026–27 tax rates.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a $90,000 salary, assuming 38 hours per week:

$90,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 = **$45.55 per hour**

This is your base rate before any casual loading or super. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust accordingly. Our [the timesheet](/) lets you type your hourly rate and see annual, weekly, and fortnightly figures instantly.

### Weekly and Fortnightly Pay

- **Weekly gross:** $90,000 ÷ 52 = $1,730.77
- **Fortnightly gross:** $1,730.77 × 2 = $3,461.54

After tax and Medicare, your weekly take-home is approximately **$1,359**. That's your **90k after tax Australia weekly salary** – the amount you actually receive in your bank account each week.

### Tax Breakdown for 2026–27

Using the resident tax scale:

- Nil tax on first $18,200
- 15% on next $26,800 ($4,020)
- 30% on next $45,000 ($13,500)
- Total tax: $17,520
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,800
- Total deductions: $19,320
- **Net annual:** $70,680
- **Net weekly:** $70,680 ÷ 52 = $1,359.23

Note: This uses the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for more details.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% loading on your base hourly rate. This is set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and is separate from super. For a $90,000 salary equivalent:

- Base hourly: $45.55
- Casual loading (25%): $11.39
- Casual hourly rate: **$56.94**

With casual loading, your weekly gross becomes $56.94 × 38 = $2,163.72, and fortnightly $4,327.44. Tax and Medicare adjust accordingly. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this interacts with awards.

### Super Guarantee: Paid on Top

Employers must pay super at 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For a $90,000 salary:

- Super contribution: $90,000 × 12% = **$10,800 per year**
- This is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27)

Super is not part of your take-home pay. It goes into your super fund. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Comparing with Minimum Wage and Awards

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual workers get $33.05 per hour including loading. A $90,000 salary is well above this, but award rates may apply to your industry. Check [pay guides](/blog) for your specific award.

### Average Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026). That's about $108,352 annually. A $90,000 salary is below this average but still above the all-employees total earnings average of $1,579.20 per week (which includes part-time workers). Remember, these are averages, not medians for your specific job. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more data.

### Fortnightly Pay Considerations

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. For a $90,000 salary:

- Fortnightly gross: $3,461.54
- Fortnightly net: $2,718.46 (approx.)

If you're casual, your fortnightly gross with loading is $4,327.44. Use our [reference tables](/data) to see how different hourly rates translate.

### Important Disclaimer

This estimate assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a precise calculation of your **90k after tax Australia weekly salary**, try our [the timesheet](/) – just enter your hourly rate and toggle casual loading. You'll see weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures with tax and super estimates.
